{{technical|date=June 2014}}

In mathematics, the '''Christ–Kiselev maximal inequality''' is a [[Maximal function|maximal inequality]] for [[filtration (mathematics)|filtrations]], named for mathematicians [[F. Michael Christ|Michael Christ]] and [[Alexander Kiselev (mathematician)|Alexander Kiselev]].<ref name="ck">M. Christ, A. Kiselev, Maximal functions associated to filtrations. J. Funct. Anal. 179 (2001), no. 2, 409--425. {{cite web |url=http://www.math.wisc.edu/~kiselev/maxim.pdf |title=Archived copy |accessdate=2014-05-12 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140514121530/http://www.math.wisc.edu/~kiselev/maxim.pdf |archivedate=2014-05-14 }}</ref>

==Continuous filtrations==
A '''continuous filtration''' of <math>(M,\mu)</math> is a family of measurable sets <math>\{A_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\mathbb{R}}</math> such that
# <math>A_\alpha\nearrow M</math>, <math>\bigcap_{\alpha\in\mathbb{R}}A_\alpha=\emptyset</math>, and <math>\mu(A_\beta\setminus A_\alpha)<\infty</math> for all <math>\beta>\alpha</math> (stratific) 
# <math>\lim_{\varepsilon\to0^+}\mu(A_{\alpha+\varepsilon}\setminus A_\alpha)=\lim_{\varepsilon\to0^+}\mu(A_\alpha\setminus A_{\alpha+\varepsilon})=0</math> (continuity)

For example, <math>\mathbb{R}=M</math> with measure <math>\mu</math> that has no pure points and

: <math>A_\alpha:=\begin{cases}\{|x|\le\alpha\},&\alpha>0, \\ \emptyset,&\alpha\le0. \end{cases}</math>

is a continuous filtration.

==Continuum version==
Let <math>1\le p<q\le\infty</math> and suppose <math>T:L^p(M,\mu)\to L^q(N,\nu)</math> is a [[bounded linear operator]] for [[Σ-finite measure|<math>\sigma-</math>finite]] <math>(M,\mu),(N,\nu)</math>. Define the Christ–Kiselev maximal function

<math>T^*f:=\sup_\alpha|T(f\chi_\alpha)|,</math>

where <math>\chi_\alpha:=\chi_{A_\alpha}</math>. Then <math>T^*:L^p(M,\mu)\to L^q(N,\nu)</math> is a bounded operator, and

<math>\|T^*f\|_q\le2^{-(p^{-1}-q^{-1})}(1-2^{-(p^{-1}-q^{-1})})^{-1}\|T\|\|f\|_p.</math>

==Discrete version==
Let <math>1\le p<q\le\infty</math>, and suppose <math>W:\ell^p(\mathbb{Z})\to L^q(N,\nu)</math> is a bounded linear operator for [[Σ-finite measure|<math>\sigma-</math>finite]] <math>(M,\mu),(N,\nu)</math>. Define, for <math>a\in\ell^p(\mathbb{Z})</math>,

: <math>(\chi_n a):=\begin{cases}a_k,&|k|\le n\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}</math>

and <math>\sup_{n\in\mathbb{Z}^{\ge0}}|W(\chi_na)|=:W^*(a)</math>. Then <math>W^*:\ell^p(\mathbb{Z})\to L^q(N,\nu)</math> is a bounded operator.

Here, <math>A_\alpha=\begin{cases}[-\alpha,\alpha],&\alpha>0\\\emptyset,&\alpha\le0\end{cases}</math>.

The discrete version can be proved from the continuum version through constructing <math>T:L^p(\mathbb{R},dx)\to L^q(N,\nu)</math>.<ref name="ck-notes">Chapter 9 - Harmonic Analysis {{cite web |url=http://www.math.caltech.edu/courses/christ-kiselev_notes.pdf |title=Archived copy |accessdate=2014-05-12 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140513155951/http://www.math.caltech.edu/courses/christ-kiselev_notes.pdf |archivedate=2014-05-13 }}</ref>

==Applications==
The Christ–Kiselev maximal inequality has applications to the [[Fourier transform]] and convergence of [[Fourier series]], as well as to the study of Schrödinger operators.<ref name="ck" /><ref name="ck-notes" />
